Preview: The rust in your water isn't just ugly. It's cooking your appliances.

---

Words I like;
Rust never sleeps, and neither does the damage it does when you ignore it.
Here's something most folks never see coming. Iron in your water doesn't just stain your sinks and tubs orange. It settles.
Every time your water heater fires up, that dissolved iron drops out of the water and sinks to the bottom of the tank. Over time it builds up as a hard, rusty sludge sitting right on top of your heating element or burner. Now your heater has to work through a blanket of that gunk just to warm your water.
What does that cost you? Higher energy bills, because your unit runs longer to hit the same temperature. Shorter tank life, because that sediment traps heat against the steel and eats it from the inside. And that rotten, metallic taste nobody wants in their coffee.
A water heater should last ten to twelve years. Iron can cut that in half.
If you already treat your iron before it reaches your tank, good on you. That was a smart call, and your heater is quietly thanking you every single day.

# Competitor Intel Brief — 2026-09-22

# Section 1 — Executive Summary

The competitive set splits into three postures this week: local full-service bundlers (Mermaid), national credibility plays (EcoWater), and warranty/lead-gen specialists (Hampton Roads). Mermaid is the sharpest local threat — it pairs water treatment with plumbing and pump work, runs four stacked promos, and leans on 1,500+ five-star reviews and its Kinetico dealership. No competitor is publishing actual system prices; everyone gates cost behind a "free water test," so the buying funnel is still won on trust and offers, not price transparency. Note: only 3 of 8 snapshots were included in this payload, and no prior-week text was captured, so week-over-week change detection was not possible.

# Section 2 — Per-competitor table

| Competitor | Hero positioning (one phrase) | Distinct services | Pricing visible? | Notable shift this week |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mermaid Water | "Test first, install right, stand behind the work" (local water + plumbing) | Water treatment + full plumbing + pump/pressure systems + commercial (DI resin, fountains); Kinetico dealer | No dollar prices, but 4 promos: $200 off heaters, $100 off first service, free install on Kinetico, free heater flush | Prior snapshot identical (title/meta) — no detectable change |
| EcoWater | "Better water starts here" — global leader, near-century of expertise | Softeners, filtration, smart-home leak/conservation tech; third-party certified; dealer network | No — routes to free water test via local dealer | No detectable change (prior = current) |
| Hampton Roads Water Services | "Full-service water quality experts" for Hampton Roads/Richmond | Water testing, hard water, bacteria/virus treatment; Lifetime Warranty; US-made (Chicago) | No — free water test as entry point | No detectable change |
| (5 competitors) | — | Snapshots not provided in this payload | — | Data missing |

# Section 3 — Implications for ClearWave

- **Counter the bundle:** Mermaid's water+plumbing+pump combo lets it own the whole home and cross-sell. Test a "water + plumbing referral partner" or add-on service so ClearWave isn't the single-purpose vendor in a head-to-head.
- **Borrow the offer stack:** Every serious competitor gates price behind a free test, but Mermaid wins attention with 3–4 concrete dollar/free promos. Pilot 1–2 crisp promos (e.g., "$X off first install," "free install on qualifying systems") to lift lead conversion.
- **Match warranty as a trust lever:** Hampton Roads leads with a "Lifetime Warranty" and floods the page with named local reviews. ClearWave should surface its strongest warranty terms and Google review count above the fold — this is the low-cost credibility battleground while no one competes on price.

- Obtain the missing 5 competitor snapshots — brief is only half-complete without them.
- Establish a real prior-week baseline; this week's "prior_snapshot" fields duplicate current data, so no change tracking is possible yet.
- Mermaid promos are stacked/rotating — watch whether the $200 heater and $100 first-service offers persist or escalate next week.
- Watch EcoWater's smart-home leak/conservation line — if a local dealer pushes it into NoVA, it's a differentiated angle ClearWave lacks.

Request → Quote is the leak — only 26.5% of 200 leads got a quote, choking ~$298K in GP off the top of the funnel while everything downstream is actually improving.
